item.title: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.

item.title: 'From socialite to shopgirl': American Girl Samantha gets a new story
item.description: As the American Girl doll company celebrates its 40th anniversary, Samantha has turned 25 — and is the subject of a new historical fiction novel by author Fiona Davis.

item.title: With an ad aimed at Trump, this Republican exposed GOP angst about Latino voters
item.description: Rep. María Elvira Salazar filmed an ad warning the president that he's "gone too far" on immigration. It reflected concern among some Republicans that their gains with Latino voters could be at risk.

item.title: French police arrest 1,800 after violent clashes and looting mar protests
item.description: Police arrested at least 1,800 people across France after violent groups clashed with officers and looted shops during nationwide demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands of people.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV leaves hospital days after lung cancer surgery
item.description: The Pope left Rome's Gemelli Hospital Saturday, days after surgery for lung cancer removed the lower lobe of his right lung. He is currently scheduled to travel to Latin America in November.

item.title: Zelenskyy urges support for new US sanctions on Russia after Trump puts them on hold
item.description: Zelenskyy described the move as unfortunate, adding it would encourage Russia to continue its assault. Trump told Congress that the pause was in the national interest but gave no further details.

item.title: Decades after apartheid, South Africans seek justice for crimes of the past
item.description:
More than three decades after the end of apartheid, families of victims of some of the worst crimes of South Africa's past
are still fighting for justice. As survivors and perpetrators grow older, a new wave of legal efforts is seeking truth, accountability and reparations before it's too late.

item.title: Sidewalk sleepers: They have nowhere else to stay while a loved one is in the hospital
item.description: Patients travel miles to be treated at public hospitals in Delhi. Those in need get financial aid for their care. But for overnight accommodations, families are often on their own — and on the street.
